meaning: Arrows run from mathematical ingredients to results that use them. This overview is curated from the papers; the Source references view displays the separate compiler-recorded relation.

companionPaper.citation: Gaspers, He and Mackenzie, “NP-Completeness of Deterministic Communication Complexity via Relaxed Interlacing” (companion manuscript, 2026).
companionPaper.leanModules: Its Lean formalization is vendored into this project as the modules NPCC.*, Workspace.*, EthBridge.* and LegacyNPCC.*, which compile as part of this build.

originCaptions.external-this-paper: EXTERNAL INPUT · THIS PAPER, NOT IN LEAN

nodes.title: Source graphs
nodes.summary: Translate a formula into one fixed list of graphs. Satisfiability and unsatisfiability give different colouring guarantees for that same list. This existence theorem is not proved in Lean: it enters the root theorem as an explicit hypothesis. Expander existence is upstream of it, not a third direct input.

provenance.statedBy: Formal paper, Assumption 4.1 (ass:finite-source), §4 “Guarded source”; reader paper §2.2 (sec:reader-external-inputs).
provenance.lean: Not proved in Lean. The Lean development states the contract (FiniteSourceRealLogSpec) and consumes a provider (FiniteSourceProvider); it never proves that a provider exists.
provenance.entersRoot: As an explicit hypothesis of the root theorem. Everything Lean proves downstream of it is conditional on it.
provenance.intendedSource: Its intended source is the companion construction: Gaspers, He and Mackenzie, “NP-Completeness of Deterministic Communication Complexity via Relaxed Interlacing” (companion manuscript, 2026). Expanders may be used to prove it; they are not a separate input.

nodes.title: Balanced families

milestone.label: Balanced families
milestone.note: external input · this paper, on paper

nodes.summary: Polynomial families supply the distribution and product estimates needed to select matrix coordinates. This existence and counting theorem is proved on paper in this paper, by an explicit polynomial construction, and is deliberately kept outside Lean.

provenance.statedBy: Formal paper, Theorem 4.4 (thm:balanced-family-realization), §4 and Appendix D; reader paper §2.3.
provenance.lean: Not proved in Lean. The Lean development states the contract (FiniteBalancedFamilySpec) and consumes a provider (FiniteBalancedFamilyProvider). The human proof — an explicit polynomial construction with an interpolation and bucket count — is in this paper.
provenance.entersRoot: As an explicit hypothesis of the root theorem, alongside the composed source theorem.
provenance.intendedSource: This paper supplies it. The companion paper's own Lean layer historically carries a balanced-family citation axiom (NPCC.M2_robust_closed → aghp_balanced_family_exists); that axiom is not in this root theorem's audited axiom footprint.

nodes.title: Choose the parameters
nodes.summary: Select one numerical schedule and a formula-independent cutoff that make every amplification step admissible.

nodes.title: Construct the matrices

milestone.label: Construction
milestone.note: stages one to four, no assignment used

nodes.summary: Build the three preliminary stages, the fourth-stage matrix, and its labelled copies without using a satisfying assignment or the satisfiability of the formula.

nodes.title: Protect the lower bound
nodes.summary: Labelled duplication preserves exact communication cost and gives lower bounds on large restrictions and on a designated reference submatrix.
nodes.companionNote: The reader appendix argues these lower bounds through the companion paper's localised extension corollary, including its two-copy and odd-copy lower bounds. In Lean that reasoning enters through the vendored companion modules listed below.

nodes.title: Align the restriction scales

milestone.label: Scale alignment
milestone.note: interlace and transpose to one threshold

nodes.summary: An interlace and transpose bring the lower bounds to a common row-density threshold, making them suitable for the next step.
nodes.companionNote: The interlacing and transposition machinery, and the localised extension corollary the reader appendix invokes, are formalized in the companion paper's Lean layer; the declarations reached there are listed below.

nodes.title: Restore robustness
nodes.summary: A general communication lemma turns the aligned bounds into a robust lower bound for an interlaced matrix. It also transports upper bounds.
nodes.companionNote: The general interlacing lemma this step applies is the companion paper's; its Lean statement and proof live in the vendored companion modules listed below, together with the localised extension corollary used in the reader appendix.

nodes.title: Add one bit to the gap
nodes.summary: Combine the construction-specific lower bound and the robustness lemma. One fixed successor gains exactly one bit in the negative case, with a matching upper bound and exact carrier sizes.
nodes.companionNote: The lower-bound half of this step runs through the companion paper's localised extension corollary and its two-copy and odd-copy bounds; the reached companion declarations are listed below.

nodes.title: Start with the full-cube matrix
nodes.summary: A rank argument gives the initial exact communication cost and the robustness needed to begin amplification.

nodes.title: Repeat the same construction

milestone.label: Iteration
milestone.note: k successors on each source graph

nodes.summary: Iterate the matrix-and-budget successor k times on each source graph. The matrices are shared by both satisfiability cases.

nodes.title: An exact k-bit gap

milestone.label: k-bit gap
milestone.note: satisfiable low, unsatisfiable budget plus k

nodes.summary: Induction gives a low-cost member when the formula is satisfiable, and exactly the prescribed budget plus k for every member when it is unsatisfiable.
nodes.companionNote: The unsatisfiable half inherits the companion paper's lower-bound apparatus, including the localised extension corollary; every companion declaration reached from this step's Lean components is listed below.

nodes.title: Bound the matrix dimensions
nodes.summary: Read dimensions from the actual successor matrices and bound their logarithms by a scalar recurrence. The fixed cutoff makes the final bound at most floor(n/(2k)).

nodes.title: Count the same matrix's entries
nodes.summary: Convert the logarithmic dimension bound into separate row and column bounds, then multiply. No padding or replacement matrix is used.

nodes.title: Communication gap and size

milestone.label: Headline theorem
milestone.note: conditional on the two external inputs

nodes.summary: For each fixed positive k, sufficiently large formulas yield one nonempty matrix family with the stated satisfiability gap and at most 2^floor(n/k) entries per matrix — conditional on the two external inputs above.

provenance.statedBy: Reader paper, Theorem 1.1; formal paper, Theorem 1.1 (thm:finite-main).
provenance.lean: Kernel-checked. The recorded axiom audit for EthInapproximability.V4.FiniteCanonicalExternalBalancednessRoot.canonical_fixedK_sameMatrix_root_of_realLogSource reports exactly propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound (verification log 07-source-log-axioms.log, published with this index).
provenance.entersRoot: This is the root theorem. It is conditional: the composed source theorem and the balanced-family theorem are explicit hypotheses, not Lean proofs.
provenance.intendedSource: Runtime, effectivity and the ETH consequence are outside the formalized scope. The companion paper's own Lean layer historically carries a balanced-family citation axiom (NPCC.M2_robust_closed → aghp_balanced_family_exists); that axiom is not in this root theorem's audited footprint.
